newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Thursday, dealers said.
They said trading was slow, with swap rates seen easing on anticipation of relatively ample liquidity on Friday following central bank dollar buying on Wednesday.
Some estimated Bank Indonesia had bought about $600 million dollar from the market to keep the dollar within its band.
But some dealers speculated for a balanced liquidity market on Friday because of anticipation of relatively large amount of maturing short-term papers (SBPUs) and weekly tax payments.
However, operators appeared to be mixed over the amount due for tax payments because some said it might not be significant as many companies will only reopen on February 17.
Indonesia was celebrating Eid al-Fitr last weekend.
But others were cautious on tax payments because of the approaching 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31. One Japanese bank dealer said banks' liquidity reports will also due Friday.
Tom/next swaps eased in mid-morning but edged up later to 2.2/2.4 points from 2.0/2.1. Overnight swaps were at 0.45/0.50.
The dealer said some selling interest was seen in dollars but the central bank floor rate seemed to limit the downside.
Spot rupiah was at 2,379.3/79.5 at 0930 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,378.0/79.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,376.80/7.30 and 2,376.25/76.75, respectively.
One-month swap was at 13.5/14.5, two at 29.0/30.0, three at 39.5/41.5 and six at 79.0/80.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,377/2,569 and the conversion band at 2,377/2,425 on Thursday after lowering the rupiah by one point on Wednesday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week and three points the previous week.
